4K Awareness Growing, But Adoption Remains Low

Reasons why people might not be adopting 4K as quickly as they would like.

  • They just got screwed over by how 3D was going to be the future of television, so they spent thousands of dollars on perfectly good televisions that have features they don't/can't use since 3D support has died out. Those 3D TV's are still good televisions that will run for a decade before someone is forced to upgrade.

  • There is no content. Sure, you can watch nature shows and be amazed at the clarity and unrealistic presentation, but after the 1 hour demo loops 8 times, what are you left with? Netflix 4K? That's great if resolution is the only thing you are looking for, but most people that spend that kind of money on equipment aren't just looking for resolution.

  • Here's my personal reason. I own a fairly large (70") television. It is a 1080p LED and it is attached to the wall in my living room. The vast majority of content being sent to it is in 720p. How long have we been in the HD era and still the content from television creators is in 720! Here recently, the news programs (local) have made the upgrade to 1080i, and I must admit, it's beautiful. That's the local news though. Most sitcoms aren't coming in at that resolution. If anyone has a television or toolset to view the incoming streams, you will notice that many people are already using television sets that exceed the standards at which content is being produced (or at least, presented).

It's similar to how Best Buy sells more product than they have in inventory every Christmas, and then blames Amazon for their low sales. You can only screw the consumer so many times before they start to take notice.
